question: What does the Lake Mainit/Kalinawan River 2007-2008 aquatic-biodiversity survey establish, and what prevents its finfish list from becoming current, waterbody-specific app presence data?

source.citation: Uy, W. H., De Guzman, A. B., Acuña, R. E., and Roa, R. L. (2015). Aquatic Biodiversity of Lake Mainit, Southern Philippines. Journal of Environment and Aquatic Resources, 3. https://doi.org/10.48031/msunjear.2015.03.01
source.access: The official MSU at Naawan JEAR article record and the full author-uploaded copy of the same article were reviewed. The official page links its PDF through Google Drive; the publicly rendered full text on ResearchGate was used for this content audit. The paper text and tables are not retained or reproduced.

waterbodiesAsReported: Kalinawan River, the lake's outlet toward Butuan Bay
studyContext.fieldPeriodConflict: Methods state August-November 2007; Table 1 is captioned as catches from August-November 2008. The paper does not reconcile these dates, so retain the source's two reported periods rather than choose one.
studyContext.evidenceMethods: The methods describe field survey and collection, fisher interviews and local-market surveys. The authors say voucher specimens were collected for surveyed fish and separately say species reportedly present without vouchers were listed. However, the 41-row Table 1 gives no row-level specimen-accession or reported-only flag, and no voucher catalog numbers are provided in the reviewed article.
studyContext.tableScope: The article says 41 finfish were identified from fishermen's catches and market surveys and titles Table 1 as finfish caught from Lake Mainit and Kalinawan River. That table pools the lake and outlet river; individual taxa are not consistently assigned to one of those waterbodies or to a capture reach.
studyContext.additionalUnidentifiedRecords: The results say at least four additional fish species remain unidentified because no voucher specimens were collected. Table 1 also contains four unidentified finfish labels; these are not named species and are not converted to taxon records.
studyContext.freshwaterAndMigratoryScope: The article reports only 11 of 41 listed finfish as freshwater, while describing the remainder as mostly migratory; it specifically notes marine species caught near Santiago and Tubay along Kalinawan River. Do not classify the entire source list as freshwater-lake fish.
studyContext.taxonomyAndStatusLimits: The article uses historical names and older references, includes numerous genus-level labels, and gives conservation labels referencing IUCN 2014. No modern taxonomic or conservation crosswalk was performed.
studyContext.geometry: A generalized resource map is included, but no taxon-specific capture coordinates or lake-versus-river location matrix was recovered. No coordinates or geometry were copied.

interpretation.safeSummary: This is a historical 2015 primary article about an aquatic inventory conducted in and around Lake Mainit and Kalinawan River. It describes multiple evidence methods and explicitly separates voucher-backed collection from reported-only species at the methods level. Its table reports 41 finfish labels from catches/markets but pools the lake and river, does not give record-level voucher provenance, uses older taxon/status references, and contains an unresolved 2007-versus-2008 sampling-year conflict.
notSupported: Current presence, abundance, catchability, harvest availability, or a complete present-day Lake Mainit or Kalinawan River checklist.
Assigning every Table 1 taxon to Lake Mainit rather than Kalinawan River, or to a specific capture point, landing site or municipality.
Treating all rows as freshwater taxa, species-level identifications, or accessioned specimens.
Treating the four unidentified finfish labels as named species or as resolved taxon records.
Using the source's historical IUCN 2014 status or introduced/native classifications as current verified status.
Current water quality, safety, legality, geometry, species diet, or bait advice.
interpretation.productUseIfEvidenceAndReviewAreResolved: A future research citation can describe the combined Lake Mainit/Kalinawan River scope and source methods. Any individual species display requires an independent current taxonomic crosswalk, record-level specimen or report provenance, an explicit lake-versus-river origin, resolution of the field-year conflict, and a separate reuse review.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Primary aquatic inventory with methods covering fish collection, interviews and markets, but pooled lake/outlet catch table, missing record-level voucher identifiers, older taxonomy and conflicting stated field years.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: The JEAR publisher page footer states all rights reserved. No item-specific open license or reuse grant was identified in the reviewed article copy. ResearchGate access to an author-uploaded copy is access for review, not permission to reproduce or publish its content. Public-app reuse is unapproved.
qualityAndRights.handling: This file records a short audit without reproducing Table 1, photographs, figures, map labels, coordinates or status classifications. No article copy is retained.
qualityAndRights.separateEvidenceLanes: Historical collected catch, fisher-reported fish, market records, current presence, taxonomic identity, species habitat, diet, current water quality, safety and legal fishing rules remain distinct evidence types.

disposition.reason: The species table pools the lake and outlet river, does not expose per-taxon specimen/report provenance or voucher accession numbers, has a 2007/2008 sampling-year discrepancy and includes unresolved genus-level and unidentified records. The publisher page provides no item-specific reuse license.

nextAction: Continue Caraga's freshwater source sweep with a later primary survey that reports taxon-by-site specimen records and accessible voucher or photo documentation. Do not reuse the pooled historical table or its dated conservation statuses as current app data.

sources.supports: Official publisher metadata, author list, abstract, publication year, DOI, official full-text link and publisher-site all-rights-reserved footer.

Author-uploaded full article copy used to review the methods, voucher/report distinction, 2007-vs-2008 date discrepancy, pooled Lake Mainit/Kalinawan finfish table, unidentified records, migratory scope and dated status citations.
